tasks.description:
Parse this literal CSV (headerless rows name,region,sales): "alice,east,80
bob,west,30
carol,east,120
dave,west,90
eve,north,60". Keep rows where sales is at least 50. Group by region and sum sales per region. Print one line: sales>=50 by region: <region>=<sum> ... with regions ordered alphabetically (east, north, west).
tasks.expected_output: sales>=50 by region: east=200 north=60 west=90

tasks.description: Start from five messy map-like records (keys id, name, age) as in-programme map literals built with mmap/mset, for example: mset (mset (mset mmap "id" "1") "name" " Alice ") "age" "30"; mset (mset (mset mmap "id" "2") "name" "Bob") "age" "25.7"; mset (mset mmap "id" "3") "age" "40" (missing name); mset (mset (mset mmap "id" "1") "name" "Alice") "age" "30" (duplicate id); mset (mset (mset mmap "id" "4") "name" "  Dana  ") "age" "" (empty age). Normalise each row: trim name (default "unknown" if missing), coerce age to a floored integer (default 0). Deduplicate by id keeping the first. Print one line: rows=<count> total_age=<sum> avg_age=<rounded mean>.

Two fixed time windows in minutes from midnight: A is 09:00–12:00 (540–720) and B is 11:00–14:00 (660–840). Compute the overlap length in minutes (0 if they do not overlap). Print exactly: overlap_min=<n>.

Given this literal list of health probes as (status_code, latency_ms): (200,120), (200,650), (503,30), (200,210), (0,0), (404,80), (200,480). Classify each: down if code is 0 or >=500 or <200; else degraded if code >=400 or latency >500; else healthy. Print one line: healthy=<n> degraded=<n> down=<n>.
